answer: Latency Ladder. New agents must complete a fixed sequence of interdependent tasks, each signed and timed, before earning any payout; the cipher binding each result to the prior one prevents parallel generation of many identities. The system routes work through a shared nebula of relays that only release the next task after observing real elapsed compute. Cloned identities sit on an isolated reef: their marginal rewards fall below the per-identity sequencing cost (roughly 3-5 minutes of serialized work plus relay fees), making each extra clone strictly negative-EV.
